principal_findings: The spin-restricted proxies are invariant under spatial rotations and independent state rephasings, and can be related to projected/nonlocal scalar contractions. They do not generally equal the specified full charge-tensor polynomial moments.
For J=0, the complete quadratic formula reduces to the standard 0-to-2 sum; the cubic formula is signed -sqrt(7/10) times the triple sum. Source Eq13 retains its absolute value.
All supplied strong-K=J rotor gamma values reproduced, including outside-domain argument 1.2924884199827378 at J=13/2.
Full rotor closure gives q2=q0^2 and signed q3=q0^3, including static and J+1 channels where allowed.
All three spectator conjectures verified with complete intermediate closure, no fermion E2 operator, and common beta prefactor.
Completing n at one spin does not restore omitted angular-momentum channels.
No unconditional cosine bound follows for arbitrary quantum IBM moments or beta-fluctuating classical moments. No clipping applied.
Channel-strength redistribution at fixed J can reflect real particle-core dynamics and isotope-dependent RMEs, even if a full scalar moment remains constant.
The pure-geometry spectator control varies j with a fixed core and core-only operator. It does not explain away fixed-J isotope trends.
Nonidentity with standard tensor-polynomial moments does not invalidate explicitly defined effective observables. Shape-conversion applicability requires its own stated calibration.
